findings.claim: The leftover-part archive now requires the old part title to end in " (part i/oldParts)". A part whose title was edited later (for example through mem_update) no longer matches, so re-saving the document shorter leaves that part active, orphaned and searchable. Ownership is decided only by the title, which a user can change.
proof_refs: base d25aae2 loop matched topic_key only

findings.claim: The moved-key branch never checks that the memory is this document part: a different memory with a moved key <key>/part-i~<digits> and a title ending in " (part i/oldParts)" with the same i and N would be archived. Needs a coincidence of key and title suffix; the title prefix is not compared with the old part 1 title and import_map is not consulted.

The OR with substr/glob on topic_key likely prevents use of the topic_key index, so each leftover index may scan the project rows inside the write transaction; bounded by project size times oldParts. Schema not inspected; cost unverified.

When the document is re-saved at a size that still needs the moved part index, write() looks up topic_key = <key>/part-i, finds the unrelated key holder and overwrites it while the moved part stays orphaned. Untested; already in the base.
